title: Plash

inlines.v: PLASH, noun [Gr. superabundant moisture.] 1. A small collection of standing water; a puddle. 2. The branch of a tree partly cut or lopped and bound to other branches. PLASH, verb intransitive To dabble in water; usually splash. PLASH, verb transitive [Latin plico, to fold.] To interweave branches; as, to plash a hedge or quicksets. [In New England, to splice.]
